title: 1 Corinthians Bible Quiz - Chapter 8
description: Ten questions on 1 Corinthians 8: knowledge and love, one God and one Lord, a weak conscience, and a stumbling block to the weak.

questions.text: What does verse 1 say about knowledge and love?
questions.explanation: The verse says knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.

answers.text: Love puffs up, but knowledge builds up
Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up
Both knowledge and love build up
Neither knowledge nor love builds up

questions.text: What does verse 2 say about anyone who thinks that he knows something?
questions.explanation: The verse says he does not yet know as he ought to know.

answers.text: He knows more than he says
He should teach the weak
He does not yet know as he ought to know
He should keep silent in the assembly

questions.text: According to verse 4, what do they know about idols?
questions.explanation: The verse says they know that no idol is anything in the world, and that there is no other God but one.

answers.text: That no idol is anything in the world
That every idol has some power
That idols belong to the Gentiles alone
That idols must be destroyed by the assembly

questions.text: Which two does verse 6 name as the one God and the one Lord?
questions.explanation: The verse says that to us there is one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom are all things.

answers.text: Moses and Jesus Christ
The Father and the Spirit
Jesus Christ and Cephas
God the Father and Jesus Christ

questions.text: What happens to the weak conscience of some who eat, according to verse 7?
questions.explanation: The verse says that their conscience, being weak, is defiled.

answers.text: It is strengthened
It is defiled
It is taken away
It is made holy

questions.text: What does verse 8 say about food?
questions.explanation: The verse says food will not commend us to God; we are no worse if we do not eat, and no better if we eat.

answers.text: It will not commend us to God
It makes us better if we eat
It makes us worse if we eat
It is forbidden to all

questions.text: What does verse 9 warn their liberty must not become?
questions.explanation: The verse warns that by no means should this liberty of theirs become a stumbling block to the weak.

answers.text: A boast among the strong
A law for the Gentiles
A reason to leave the assembly
A stumbling block to the weak

questions.text: Where does verse 10 say a weak person might see someone who has knowledge sitting?
questions.explanation: The verse speaks of a man who sees you who have knowledge sitting in an idol's temple.

answers.text: At the table of the assembly
In the market
In an idol's temple
At a wedding feast

questions.text: According to verse 12, whom do they sin against by wounding a weak brother's conscience?
questions.explanation: The verse says that in sinning against the brothers and wounding their weak conscience, you sin against Christ.

answers.text: Christ
The assembly
Themselves only
The idol

questions.text: What does the writer say he will do if food causes his brother to stumble?
questions.explanation: Verse 13 says he will eat no meat forever more, so that he does not cause his brother to stumble.

answers.text: He will eat only at home
He will teach his brother to eat
He will eat no meat forever more
He will leave the city
